note: 拜火祠、祭司的净室 (native:fanfang/fire_hall, priest_room; 番坊 B): a dark hall of black stone glossed by three hundred years of smoke, one thing in it — the chest-high black altar in the middle with the fire on it, no wood, no oil, the smoke going up through the square hole in the roof (a shaft of light falls back down it by day); the stone before the altar worn white by knees; a water vat for the washing of hands, a stone bench by the door, jars of oil nobody has seen used. East the priest's bare cell: a narrow couch, a chest, a lamp, the black slab with a flame cut in it, not a speck of dust. Old and used: soot up every wall, ash drifted round the altar's foot, the white kneeling-place; the cell swept clean to the point of strangeness.
